statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The cash-session selloff leaves residual Tail elevated immediately after the close, while the afternoon rebound argues against a high-band reading.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES; residual post-close Tail is elevated, with higher-band risk contingent on renewed extension or failed retracements.
headline: Post-close Tail remains elevated after a rates-led technology decline, but mean reversion from the afternoon low limits the band.
body: The U.S. cash session ended after a broad technology selloff driven by higher Treasury yields and firmer oil. Late-session NQ evidence remained bearish and in the lower part of the day’s range, but price had rebounded materially from the intraday low. That combination supports elevated rather than high Tail.

lookbackSummary: Tail was low through the overnight and pre-open periods, moved to WATCH at 14:00 UTC, then remained elevated from 15:00 through 19:00 UTC as the rates-led technology decline persisted.
outlookSummary: Residual Tail is elevated immediately after the close but should normalize if futures rotate and hold above the afternoon low. The next major conditional risk cluster is Thursday’s U.S. data and cash-open window; scheduled events raise Stress first, with Tail dependent on the observed price path.

forecast.analysis: Low Tail becomes the baseline if futures continue two-way rotation and the rates impulse stops intensifying; a fresh directional break would invalidate that path.
Early-evening risk stays low if futures remain balanced. Thin liquidity can raise noise, but it is not itself evidence of persistent mean-reversion failure.
The overnight transition favors low Tail if retracements remain available and no new geopolitical or rates shock creates directional efficiency.
Low Tail persists if overnight futures rotate around value; repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the main reason to re-rate higher.
Quiet overnight trade keeps Tail low unless a new catalyst produces sustained one-way NQ structure rather than a temporary gap or headline move.
The low-Tail baseline holds if price discovery remains two-way; cross-asset moves matter only if they align with persistent NQ direction.
Tail remains low in the pre-Europe window unless futures begin holding near an overnight extreme with shallow retracements.
Tail edges slightly higher into the Europe handoff if liquidity broadens around an already directional move; balanced trade would keep risk low.
Early-European risk remains modest unless NQ direction aligns with renewed pressure from yields, oil, semiconductors or megacaps.
Tail stays low-to-moderate through Europe if overnight extremes are not repeatedly extended and pullbacks remain meaningful.
The European morning remains a low-Tail baseline; persistent directional efficiency would be needed before the U.S. data window to justify a higher band.
Risk stays contained if NQ remains rotational ahead of the U.S. calendar. Event proximity raises Stress more readily than Tail before outcomes are known.
Tail remains low approaching U.S. premarket if price structure is balanced; a one-way premarket move with poor retracements would increase path risk.
WATCH becomes appropriate as the U.S. release window approaches, but Tail remains conditional on observed NQ structure rather than scheduled events alone.
The 08:30 ET international-transactions release and 08:50 ET Hammack remarks raise event/whipsaw Stress. Tail stays WATCH unless the actual reaction becomes persistent.
The cash-open hour carries WATCH-level Tail conditionally. A gap that extends with shallow or failed pullbacks would be the trigger for an elevated reading.
The 10:00 ET New Residential Sales release overlaps early cash-session discovery. Elevated Tail is conditional on persistent post-release extension and weak retracements.
Tail falls back to WATCH if the first post-data hour develops two-way trade; repeated extension after failed rebounds would keep the elevated scenario active.
Midday Tail remains WATCH if residual directional pressure persists, but meaningful retracements and cross-asset stabilization would support further normalization.
WATCH persists into early afternoon only if the morning directional impulse remains unresolved; balanced rotation would reduce path risk.
Low Tail is the baseline if afternoon trade is two-way and no new catalyst creates a second directional leg.
Late-afternoon Tail remains low if price discovery is balanced; a fresh extreme-holding move with failed retracements would be the main invalidation.
